20280104000000_operational_incident_plat.evidence: ADM-013 PHASE 4 — PLATFORM INCIDENT UNIQUENESS. Adds one partial unique index, `operational_incidents_platform_fingerprint_uk ON operational_incidents (fingerprint) WHERE team_id IS NULL`. No column is added, altered or dropped; no row is read, written or deleted. EXPAND-only and safe before code deployment: the index enforces an invariant the writer already assumes, so applying it ahead of the code narrows a window rather than opening one. WHY IT IS NEEDED: `@@unique([teamId, fingerprint])` does not deduplicate platform-scope rows at all — a standard Postgres unique index treats NULL as distinct from NULL, so (NULL,'x') and (NULL,'x') are two keys. Measured against a fully-migrated PostgreSQL 16 before the migration was written: both rows insert with no error. Every PLATFORM and LEGACY_UNSCOPED incident has therefore been un-deduplicated since the column became nullable. WHY IT CARRIES NO BACKFILL AND NO DELETE: a unique index cannot be created over existing duplicates, so a database carrying them must converge FIRST. Convergence merges and deletes rows, which is irreversible, and `full-migration-audit.mjs` classifies DELETE_FROM in a post-baseline migration as CRITICAL with no guarded form. The two halves are split by AUDIENCE: this migration is safe unattended, and `services/api/scripts/incident-convergence.mjs` merges duplicates after a reviewed dry-run and an explicit operator decision. BEHAVIOUR ON A DIRTY DATABASE: it RAISES, naming the duplicate group count, the excess row count and the exact commands to run — it does not skip. A silent skip would leave the invariant unenforced on precisely the database that needed it while the deploy went green. REHEARSED against live PostgreSQL 16: applies on a clean database (index present); refuses on a database seeded with 2 duplicate groups / 3 excess rows, with the remediation in DETAIL and HINT; and after `incident-convergence.mjs --apply` plus `prisma migrate resolve --rolled-back`, re-deploys cleanly with the index present. Idempotent — `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`, and a no-op when the operator script created the index first.
